mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 3% may signal tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 3% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases, it signals a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS improve but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased demand, which may positively affect S&P 500 returns in a late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative during late-cycle expansion more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Higher consumer price index (CPI) may lead to inflation, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate below 3.5% may indicate a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 3.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both industrial production and retail sales suggests strong economic supply, positively affecting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both INDPRO and RSAFS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rate may negatively impact S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises during tightening but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.
